title: 6 March 1964: Filming: A Hard Day's Night
content:
Day five of the filming for A Hard Day’s Night, The Beatles’ debut feature film.

As on the previous three days, the group boarded a train at Acton Main Line in west London, to film railway scenes for the early part of the film. On this day their train travelled between London and Newton Abbot in the county of Devon.

Page last updated: 30 March 2010

Also on this day...

  • 2015: Ringo Starr and his All-Starr Band live: Centro Comercial Bima Outlet Autopista Norte, Bogotá
  • 1999: Ringo Starr and his All-Starr Band live: Konocti Harbor, Kelseyville
  • 1975: Recording: Rock Show, You Gave Me The Answer, Listen To What The Man Said by Wings
  • 1973: Recording: You’re Sixteen, Oh My My by Ringo Starr
  • 1972: Recording: Big Barn Bed by Wings
  • 1972: John Lennon and Yoko Ono receive US deportation notice
  • 1970: Mixing: Sentimental Journey by Ringo Starr
  • 1970: Recording: You Always Hurt The One You Love by Ringo Starr
  • 1970: UK single release: Let It Be
  • 1967: Recording, mixing: Sgt Pepper’s Lonely Hearts Club Band
  • 1966: Paul McCartney and Jane Asher holiday in Switzerland
  • 1965: Filming: Help!, the Bahamas
  • 1963: Radio: Here We Go
  • 1962: The Beatles live: Cavern Club, Liverpool (evening)
  • 1961: The Beatles live: Liverpool Jazz Society, Liverpool
  • 1961: The Beatles live: Cavern Club, Liverpool (lunchtime)
